args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1, the service failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging, so this release should probably not have reached production.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. I rolled all three regions back to it.
- **Check after rollback:** all regions now run v2.3.0, the service is passing health checks, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It explains what failed and that I rolled back. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before anyone redeploys it.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
